source.check: unopposed members and full names from the News-Letter's list of nominations (6 May; * = retiring member as printed there) and its list of the remaining contests after withdrawals (7 May); votes, majorities, spoiled papers and electorates read on the page image of the News-Letter's results

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934 (no election in January 1935): one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the 1932 cohort) and the eight aldermen elected in 1929 (Clifton, Court, Cromac, Dock, Falls, Shankill, Victoria, Windsor); nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. After the withdrawal in Dock, 17 of the 23 seats were filled unopposed; Clifton, Court (both seats), Duncairn, Falls and Smithfield were contested (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 7 and 16 May 1936). Malcolm Mercer, the retiring councillor, withdrew his councillorship nomination by arrangement with the Independent Unionists (News-Letter, 6 May 1936); the 7 May list labels Johnston Independent and the nomination list says the Unemployed Workers' Movement.
